item.title: Or when there is sloth and torpor internally, he understands: 'There is sloth and torpor in me'; or when there is no sloth and torpor…
item.description:
Or when there is sloth and torpor internally, he understands: 'There is sloth and torpor in me'; or when there is no sloth and torpor internally, he understands: 'There is no sloth and torpor in me.' And he understands how unarisen sloth and torpor arises; and he understands how arisen sloth and torpor is abandoned; and he understands how abandoned sloth and torpor will not arise in the future.

From: Dīgha Nikāya 22 – Mahāsatipaṭṭhānasutta

item.title: Elder Nun Upacālā: Mindful, with the Dhamma-eye, A bhikkhunī training the faculties, Penetrates the peaceful path, Practiced by the supreme person. Why do you not…
item.description:
Elder Nun Upacālā:

Mindful, with the Dhamma-eye,
A bhikkhunī training the faculties,
Penetrates the peaceful path,
Practiced by the supreme person.

Why do you not like birth?
One born enjoys sensual pleasures.
Enjoy sensual pleasures,
Do not regret it later.

One who is born is subject to death,
Hands and feet are cut off,
Killed, bound, afflicted.
Afterwards, suffering comes.

Born in the Sakya clan,
The Buddha, the undefeated one,
Taught me the Dhamma,
To overcome birth.

He taught the Noble Eightfold Path,
About suffering, the origin of suffering,
About overcoming suffering,
And the path to the end of suffering.

Having heard his words,
I live delighting in the teaching.
I have attained the three knowledges,
Done is the Buddha's teaching.

Everywhere, joy is destroyed,
The mass of delusion is shattered.
Know thus, Evil One!
You are defeated, O Death.

From: Therīgāthā 7.3

item.title: Then the Venerable Sāriputta went to the Blessed One, paid homage, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the Venerable Sāriputta said:…
item.description:
Then the Venerable Sāriputta went to the Blessed One, paid homage, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the Venerable Sāriputta said: 'Venerable Sir, this entire holy life is good friendship, good companionship, good association.' - 'Good, good, Sāriputta! This entire holy life is good friendship, good companionship, good association. Sāriputta, for a bhikkhu with good friends, good companions, good associates, it can be expected that the Noble Eightfold Path will be developed, that the Noble Eightfold Path will be cultivated.'

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 45.3

item.title: Furthermore, bhikkhus, with sensual desire as cause, with sensual desire as condition, with sensual desire as reason, with sensual desire itself as cause, they engage…
item.description:
Furthermore, bhikkhus, with sensual desire as cause, with sensual desire as condition, with sensual desire as reason, with sensual desire itself as cause, they engage in misconduct of body, misconduct of speech, misconduct of mind. Having engaged in misconduct of body, speech, and mind, after death, with the breakup of the body, they are reborn in a plane of misery, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell. Bhikkhus, such is the danger of sensual desires, bringing suffering in the future, a mass of suffering, with sensual desire as cause, with sensual desire as condition, with sensual desire as source, with sensual desire as reason.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 13 – Mahādukkhakkhandhasutta

item.title: - Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu reviles, criticizes, and scolds the noble ones and his fellow celibates, it is impossible, it cannot happen that he will…
item.description:
- Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu reviles, criticizes, and scolds the noble ones and his fellow celibates, it is impossible, it cannot happen that he will not encounter one of these ten misfortunes. What ten? He does not attain what has not been attained; what has been attained declines; he does not become well-versed in the good Dhamma; he becomes over-conceited regarding the good Dhamma; he does not live the holy life with joy; he commits a corrupt offense; he experiences a severe illness; he becomes mentally deranged; he becomes confused at the time of death; or after death, with the breakup of the body, he is reborn in a plane of misery, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell. Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu reviles, criticizes, and scolds the noble ones and his fellow celibates, it is impossible, it cannot happen that he will not encounter one of these ten misfortunes.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 10.88

item.title: Friends, if others should treat a bhikkhu who is not perfect, not good, not pleasant, by touching him with hands, with stones, with sticks, or…
item.description:
Friends, if others should treat a bhikkhu who is not perfect, not good, not pleasant, by touching him with hands, with stones, with sticks, or with swords, he understands thus: 'Such is the nature of this body that hands can touch it, stones can touch it, sticks can touch it, swords can touch it. The Blessed One has said in the simile of the saw: "Bhikkhus, even if low-down bandits were to saw your limbs one by one with a two-handled saw, yet if anyone among you defiled his mind, that person would not be following my teaching." I will be energetic and diligent, not lazy. Mindfulness is established without confusion, my body is tranquil, not agitated, my mind is concentrated and unified. Now let hands touch this body, let stones touch this body, let sticks touch this body, let swords touch this body — the teaching of the Buddhas must be practiced.'

From: Majjhima Nikāya 28 – Mahāhatthipadopamasutta

item.title: Householder, that noble disciple, having known that sensual desire is a defilement of the mind, abandons sensual desire, the defilement of the mind; having known…
item.description:
Householder, that noble disciple, having known that sensual desire is a defilement of the mind, abandons sensual desire, the defilement of the mind; having known that hatred is a defilement of the mind, abandons hatred, the defilement of the mind; having known that dullness and drowsiness are defilements of the mind, abandons dullness and drowsiness, the defilements of the mind; having known that restlessness and remorse are defilements of the mind, abandons restlessness and remorse, the defilements of the mind; having known that doubt is a defilement of the mind, abandons doubt, the defilement of the mind. This, householder, is called a noble disciple of great wisdom, of wide wisdom, one who has entered the domain of clear vision, possessed of wisdom. This is called being complete in wisdom.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.61

item.title: Craving, bhikkhus, is a net that makes the wandering in saṃsāra spread out, sticky; it is because of that craving that this world is destroyed,…
item.description:
Craving, bhikkhus, is a net that makes the wandering in saṃsāra spread out, sticky; it is because of that craving that this world is destroyed, bound, tangled like a ball of thread, like a matted cocoon, like twisted muñja grass and babhaja reeds, unable to escape from the plane of misery, the bad destination, the lower realm, birth and death.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.199

item.title: Sātāgira: The sage's mind is fully accomplished, His deeds are perfectly done. Let us approach the Venerable Gotama, Fully possessed of wisdom and good conduct.…
item.description:
Sātāgira:
The sage's mind is fully accomplished,
His deeds are perfectly done.
Let us approach the Venerable Gotama,
Fully possessed of wisdom and good conduct.

Hemāvata:
His calves are like an antelope's, lean and steady,
With little food, not greedy, absorbed in jhāna.
Let us go and see the seer Gotama
Who practices jhāna in the remote forest.

Alone, like a lion, like an elephant, not grasping at pleasures,
Let us approach and ask him about release from the snare of death.

From: Sutta Nipāta 1.9

item.title: Bhikkhus, there are these five benefits for a patient person. What five? People love him and like him; no one hates him; not many people…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, there are these five benefits for a patient person. What five? People love him and like him; no one hates him; not many people avoid him; at the time of death his mind is not confused; after death, with the breakup of the body, he is reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. Bhikkhus, these are the five benefits for a patient person.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.215
